open.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: You're on my ground. Didn't post it, but it's mine, and that's the chapel's, and nobody's on that.
Deer come through the gap by the culvert. Forty years. I know what comes through the gap.
Stand faces the chapel. Deer come through the gap. He's not watching the gap.

passives.line: Four shells under the stand, not two. You don't say it yet.
His safety's off. He isn't pointing it anywhere. He hasn't put it on in days.
He says 'my ground' the way a man says it when the ground's stopped feeling like his.

options.text: What are you really hunting, Carl?
That stand's twenty yards off the chapel. You could hit the roof from there.

fail.line: You could. I could. Ain't nobody said anybody did. Deer come through the gap.

hunting.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: ...Something stood up on that roof Monday like a man off his knees. I put the glass on it. It put its eyes on me.
They lit with nothing to light 'em. Deer. Say deer when you write it down.
Eyeshine needs a source. There's no source out there.

twenty.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: Twenty yards. Yeah. I measured it with a tape, Tuesday, in daylight, 'cause I needed to know I hadn't missed.
He measured it. In daylight. With a tape.

climb.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: (The stand creaks. He shifts over without looking.)
Roof's bare. Every roof on 62 has snow but that one. Watch it a while. Then tell me about deer.
Bare and steaming. In February. I want a thermometer on that roof.

hub.speaker: r62_hunter
hub.prompt: He keeps the glass on the roof.
lines: Talk quiet. It hears quiet fine, but talk quiet.

static.line: His finger's inside the guard. It's been inside the guard since you climbed up. Don't move sudden and don't ask him why.

options.text: Four shells, Carl. You went back.
It never turned around. That's what scares you. Not that it was there.
The prints stop at the wall.
Deer season's been over since December.

back.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: ...Tuesday. I went back Tuesday. Two more. It was on the roof again and it never even turned.
Thing about twenty yards is you can't say you missed. So I've got nothing to say.
The roof was steaming. He hasn't said that yet. He will.

back_fail.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: Pick 'em up and count 'em if you want. Then put 'em back where you found 'em, 'cause they're mine.

never_turned.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: I shot it twice and it didn't care. That's not being hunted. That's not being anything. I've put down dogs that looked at me more.
I keep coming up here 'cause if it looks at me once, just once, I'll know I'm here.
He's not hunting it. He's asking it to see him.

never_fail.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: You want to know what scares a man, go stand on that roof and wait. Ab Whitmore's dog waited on his barn roof. Ask Ab how that went.

passives.line: You named the thing before he could. A man wants to be the one to say it. The ladder's cold on the way down.

prints.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: (He looks at the cast a long time.) Nine feet. I paced it. Nine feet and then nothing, like it went up the wall.
It went up the wall. I watched it go up the wall Monday, and I told myself it went round.
Ab's got barn owls in that steeple. Ab'll tell you owls. Ab wasn't on this stand.
Owls don't pace nine feet, dear. Neither does anything else on this road.

season.speaker: r62_hunter
lines: Since December. Warden knows. Drove by Wednesday and waved and kept driving.
Nobody on this road wants me to come down. I'm the one watching. Long as I'm watching, they can sleep.
A one-man neighbourhood watch, for a neighbourhood that won't say what it's watching for.
